claims.reasoning: PASS. M_COLLAPSE_TILE_BYTES=32768 is used in exactly ONE executable line (triton.py:1168) as the NUMERATOR of an integer division by feat_bytes = feature_footprint*itemsize -- the resident [inner,*features] tile footprint in bytes. It is NEVER an operand of an equality/threshold/membership/startswith fence against any kernel fact (grep over helion/ confirms the only non-comment occurrences are the assignment and the division). EQUAL-FOOTPRINT DIVERGENCE TEST (the core bar): kernels A (col_energy: 1 accumulator, grid M=4096, fp32) and B (col_mean_abs: 2 accumulators + per-row abs intermediate, grid M=8192, fp32) are structurally distinct (different grid extent, different body, different accumulator count) yet BOTH have feature_footprint=1024, itemsize=4 -> feat_bytes=4096 -> inner_byte_cap=8; a fp16 variant C' with matched footprint also gets cap=8. Seed-path trace confirms both kernels actually fire triton_reduction_user_tile and the live get_seed_config calls _m_collapse_inner_byte_cap(4096)=8, emitting an inner block_size of 8 for both. The cap bites by RESIDENCY (feat_bytes), identically for any kernel with that footprint, NOT by which kernels were measured -- exactly as claimed. The cap also MOVES across the footprint sweep (6 distinct values), so it is a genuine byte-budget, not a degenerate constant. MISCLASSIFICATION ATTEMPT (honest failure): kernel B holds TWO simultaneously-live accumulators, so its true resident footprint is ~2x A's, yet feature_footprint=1024 counts only ONE feature-axis extent and the budget gives B the SAME cap as A -- arguably B should want a smaller inner tile. This is a real granularity/SIGNAL limitation, but it is NOT a fence: the cap function gives the SAME answer for the SAME feat_bytes deterministically for any kernel; the only 'wrong' tile arises because the upstream feature_footprint fact (computed in device_ir.py, a SEPARATE fact) under-counts multi-accumulator bodies -- it does not arise from M_COLLAPSE_TILE_BYTES keying on kernel identity or a measured set. A fence would return DIFFERENT caps for the SAME footprint keyed on which kernel it is; this returns identical caps. So misclassify-as-a-fence FAILED (success would have required equal feat_bytes -> different cap, which is impossible since the cap is a pure function of feat_bytes alone). The constant is a factor inside a hardware-unit (bytes) budget, not a fact-vs-literal fence.
